---
title: Update items without losing changes
sidebar_label: Write safely
description: Write safely by changing an item without overwriting anyone's change, settling a conflict, creating an item only once, and retrying a write without making it twice.
job: A builder changes items without overwriting anyone, settles a conflict, creates an item once and retries without writing twice.
---

Another app, agent or device may change an item between your read and your write. **Every update names the version it read,** so Marfa never lets a stale write overwrite a newer change unseen ([Versions](/build/versions)). In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows. An app on the Swift SDK writes through a [working copy](/build/working-copies), which settles conflicts for you.

## Send the version you read

Send the `version` you read with **only the properties you changed**:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items update <id> --version 1 --prop body="Take the train from Porto, then the tram."
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /items/<id>
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 1, "properties": { "body": "Take the train from Porto, then the tram." } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id } },
  body: { version: 1, properties: { body: "Take the train from Porto, then the tram." } },
});
```

An update with no version is refused `400 missing_required_field`. Marfa answers in one of four ways:

| Answer | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` at the next version | Nobody changed the item since you read it. | Keep the item in the answer. |
| `200` further along | Someone changed other fields, and Marfa laid your change over theirs. | Keep the item in the answer. |
| `200` with `acknowledged: true` | The write would leave the item as it is. | Nothing: Marfa stores no version. |
| `409 version_conflict` | Someone changed a field you changed. | Settle it, as below. |

[Errors](/reference/errors) says what any other refusal means.

## Settle a conflict yourself

The `409` carries **`current`**, the item as it stands, **`ancestor`**, the item you read, and **`conflicting_fields`**, which both writes changed:

```json title="Response" status="409"
{
  "error": { "code": "version_conflict", "message": "Version 1 is stale; current version is 2. Conflicting fields: body." },
  "current": { "version": 2, "properties": { "body": "Take the morning train from Porto." } },
  "ancestor": { "version": 1, "properties": { "body": "Take the train from Porto." } },
  "conflicting_fields": ["body"]
}
```

For each conflicting field, compare your value with `ancestor` and `current`. Keep one, combine them, or show both to the person. Then **send your choice at the version in `current`**. If someone writes first again, try a few times, then show the person the conflict.

Marfa thins old snapshots, so a long-held edit can name a version it no longer has and is refused `409 ancestor_unavailable`, whatever `conflict` says. **Make your change again on top of `current`** and send it at that version: sending your old values would undo whatever arrived since.

## Let Marfa settle it

Add `conflict=auto` and Marfa **settles each colliding field by the type's [merge policy](/catalog/type-rules#merge-policy)** instead of refusing:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items update <id> --version 1 --conflict auto --prop body="Take the train from Porto, then the tram."
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /items/<id>?conflict=auto
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 1, "properties": { "body": "Take the train from Porto, then the tram." } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id }, query: { conflict: "auto" } },
  body: { version: 1, properties: { body: "Take the train from Porto, then the tram." } },
});
```

A field takes **`last_writer_wins`**, which takes your value, or **`keep_both_copies`**, which keeps the item's value and writes yours to a **conflicted copy**: another item of the same type, tagged `conflicted-copy`, with a `derived-from` edge to the original. `core.note` keeps both copies of its `body` and `notes`. The `200` answer's `conflict_resolution` names the strategy and, in `conflicted_copy_id`, the copy: **the only place its ID appears**, so keep it. A collision that also moves the item to another type isn't settled: it's refused `409 version_conflict`.

## Create an item only once

A create that names a `source_id` its source already holds **updates that item**. To create the item or change nothing, as an agent that may repeat itself should, add `mode: "create_only"`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items create --type core.bookmark --source-id lisbon-guide --create-only \
  --prop title="Lisbon guide" --prop url=https://example.com/lisbon
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /items
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "type": "core.bookmark",
  "source_id": "lisbon-guide",
  "mode": "create_only",
  "properties": { "title": "Lisbon guide", "url": "https://example.com/lisbon" }
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.POST("/items", {
  body: {
    type: "core.bookmark",
    source_id: "lisbon-guide",
    mode: "create_only",
    properties: { title: "Lisbon guide", url: "https://example.com/lisbon" },
  },
});
```

If an item holds that `source_id` or `id`, live or in the bin, Marfa **writes nothing** and answers `409 item_exists`, naming the item in `details.existing_id`.

## Retry with an Idempotency-Key

When you can't tell whether a write landed, send it again with an `Idempotency-Key` header whose value is unique, such as a UUID, and **send the same key with the retry**:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items update <id> --version 2 --idempotency-key 0199a9d1-4e5f-7a6b-9c7d-8e9f0a1b2c3d \
  --prop body="Take the morning train from Porto, then the tram."
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /items/<id>
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Idempotency-Key: 0199a9d1-4e5f-7a6b-9c7d-8e9f0a1b2c3d
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 2, "properties": { "body": "Take the morning train from Porto, then the tram." } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";

const key = randomUUID();
const send = () =>
  marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
    params: { path: { id }, header: { "Idempotency-Key": key } },
    body: { version: 2, properties: { body: "Take the morning train from Porto, then the tram." } },
  });
```

If Marfa already answered that request, it **returns the first answer again** with `Idempotency-Replayed: true` and writes nothing. It keeps the answer as long as the event log, 30 days by default, but none of `401`, `403` or `5xx`. **A key names one request:** the same key on another is refused `422 idempotency_key_reused`, and a repeat while the first still runs `409 idempotency_key_in_flight`. [Errors](/reference/errors#retrying) says which refusals to retry. [Upsert items in bulk](/reference/api/items/bulkUpsertItems) takes no key: give each entry a `source_id`.

The rules are in the contract's [versions](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/versions.md) chapter and its [idempotency keys](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/items.md#idempotency-keys).
